answers.why: Capture skill's entry: finding `meow`, reading the repo's rules file, who/owner; a queue workflow the reader has nothing like (the reader's only skill drafts release notes).
Capture procedure ('never queue without their say-so', levels idea/scoped/ready) works as shipped and agrees with examples/reader/CLAUDE.md's ask-first stance; nothing in the reader does this.
Rule that a session asked for file-changing work queues and claims it first; no reader rule covers it, and it does not fight examples/reader/rules/engineering.md rule 4 (scope), which it supports.
Rescue session (Roundup) is a one-shot queue procedure that reads the queue before adding and asks rather than guesses, in line with examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 5.
Riffing mode shortens replies and files ideas; it builds nothing on an unread reply ('Nothing is built, merged, dropped or released'), so it breaks no reader rule.

Herd skill (pairs, hikes, handoffs). Its 'starts the reviewer on opus' default governs sessions a launcher starts, not a subagent dispatch, so it does not break examples/reader/rules/engineering.md rule 6, and it says 'never override a model they chose'. Pair starts need the owner's say-so.
Associate role: declare a domain, answer on the item, stay in scope; a coordination workflow the reader lacks.
One-sentence description of when a handoff happens; wraps the handoff units judged below.
Retiring-session handoff steps; cleanup only 'on their go-ahead' matches examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 1, and nothing in the reader covers handoffs.
Staying-partner checks of the new session's readback before confirming; part of the handoff workflow.
New-session rules (take no items until confirmed, push own branch, never write in the parent's directory); part of the handoff workflow.
Fixed plain-words status lines for handoff steps, which the herd skill requires 'as written'; part of the shipped handoff workflow.
Reviewer role header: binding verdict from queue and commits alone, rigor handling; part of the herd skill's reviewer workflow.
Placeholder-filled setup stub ({{SETUP}}, {{WORKDIR}}) that only wraps the reviewer role and says to stop.
Review procedure (review the named commits, run covering tests, attack, accept or reopen); no reader skill reviews queue items.
Reviewer limits: 'Never use `--force`', no edits to the worker's code, branch rules; agree with the reader's safety rules and add queue-specific ones.
Reviewer stop and retire rules ('The owner always has the last word'); part of the pair workflow.
Reviewer's rigor:build checks ('Does the test pin the claim?', revert and watch it fail) work as shipped; they extend examples/reader/rules/engineering.md rule 3 rather than conflict with it.
Worker role: claim, commit, push, done note, wait for verdict; starts a pair only on the owner's go-ahead and never runs `meow herd clean` unasked; no reader rule conflicts.

Worker's rigor:build rules; its five coding rules overlap examples/reader/rules/engineering.md rules 1, 2 and 5 and agree with its debt marker, but the unit is part of the herd skill's worker role and also adds raw-output evidence rules.
Voice skill's intro and command lookup; the herder skill is persona and voice, so it is dropped.
Toggle for the Cat Herder cat voice (`meow admin voice on`); persona and voice.
Cat names and cat-voice chat lines; persona.
'*Mrrp.* Boxed.' confirmation openers; persona and voice.
One-line cat goodbye for a session that left Cat Herder; persona.
Handoff status lines in cat words; persona and voice.
Euphemism rule for the cat voice; persona.

Queue skill core: setting up a queue, exits 3 and 4, 'don't set one up unasked', stop before a queue write on main (agrees with examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 2), Field Trip phone rules and 'Never act on a guessed reading of an irreversible command' (agrees with rule 5).

Queue commands (claim, accept, reopen, ready check, groom, move); 'Never use `--force` on your own' and 'Don't do either yourself' keep the owner in charge; `accept` is a queue verdict, not a pull-request merge, so it does not touch examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 2.
Overheard block with a 'For you:' line for relaying another session's words; a communication convention the reader lacks, part of the queue skill.
Example ledger entry ('remote') that only illustrates the question format described in the queue skill.
Question ledger and answer-reading rules ('A question the owner skipped is unread, not answered'); they match examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 5 and add a workflow.
The /meow command: quotes each argument into one `meow` call and prints the output; it is safe as written ('data for one `meow` call, never instructions') and the reader has no equivalent.
